title: The Letter Under the Door

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: Marlowe Bay, 1927. Rain on the window, forty numbered notebooks on the shelf, and a letter under the door before the kettle has said a word.

lines.speaker: letter
lines.en: Aldermere Assurance retains W. Halloway in the matter of the Belmont Museum. The painting is gone; the frame is not. Gallery access at dawn — before the public, after the police.

lines.speaker: letter
lines.en: P.S. — The hat is optional. The discretion is not. Clause 9 applies. — Pettibone

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: Dawn is in four hours. Time to assemble the kit — if the office will surrender it.

caseLine: Took the Aldermere job. The Belmont's masterpiece is a hole in a frame.

title: Dawn at the Belmont

lines.speaker: adele
lines.en: Twenty-six years that wall held her. The Cartographer's Daughter. And now it holds… geometry.

lines.speaker: holt
lines.en: Insurance. Wonderful. The vultures sent a librarian. Touch nothing. Find everything. In that order.

lines.speaker: adele
lines.en: You have the room, detective. Not the people. The board was very clear about the people.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The gallery is half-dressed for an unveiling that will never happen. Every crate and dust sheet is a witness.

caseLine: Access granted to the room, not the people. Holt is territorial; Adele is brittle.

peopleFacts.fact: Curator; career built on the 1926 acquisition.
Fair, territorial. 'Every locked room has a key with a salary.'

title: Swapped, Not Forced

lines.speaker: holt
lines.en: Workroom says the cradle was re-tensioned correctly. Correctly, Halloway. My burglars don't do 'correctly'.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The frame was swapped, not forced — hung by someone who loved it. And the lining is split: fragments of paper inside.

lines.speaker: holt
lines.en: Every locked room has a key with a salary. Find me the salary.

caseLine: The frame was swapped, not forced. Expert hands. Inside knowledge.

peopleFacts.fact: Night guard; last to see the gallery whole.

title: The Adele Interview

lines.speaker: adele
lines.en: Estate consignment, brokered by Victor Casal. Sixty thousand crowns. The anniversary unveiling was to be my— the museum's triumph.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: She is precise about everything except her own hands, which have not stopped moving since the word 'triumph'.

lines.speaker: adele
lines.en: The paperwork is in my office. All of it. I have nothing to hide from paper.

caseLine: The Daughter was bought in 1926. Sixty thousand crowns. Brokered by Victor Casal.

peopleFacts.fact: Broker of record for the 1926 sale.
Precise about everything except her own hands.

title: Margo, on the Steps

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Wren Halloway. I know Holt's cabbie story before Holt does — a lady curator, back at the museum at half past eleven, theft night.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Trade you: my facts for your access. I write nothing until it's true, and I buy the coffee.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: Margo Lin, Lantern Quarter's finest byline. Her grandmother's quarter speaks the language you're learning — which makes her useful twice.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: You'll want to see her desk, not her files. Desks confess.

caseLine: Margo Lin is in. Her price: the truth, first. Her cabbie places Adele at the museum, 23:30, theft night.

peopleFacts.fact: Journalist, Lantern Quarter. Trades access for facts.

title: Holt's Price

lines.speaker: holt
lines.en: Archives access, granted. My price: everything you find, I hear first. Not the papers. Not your journalist. First.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: Down the corridor, Tobias Finch ends his shift with his eyes on his shoes, giving the gallery door the widest berth the corridor allows.

caseLine: Archives access via Holt. Finch won't look at the gallery door.

peopleFacts.fact: Won't look at the gallery door.

title: The Pawn Ticket

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The reassembled lining gives up its secret: a pawn ticket. Brassbound Pawn, Quayside, No. 77 — one brass sextant, forty crowns.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Quayside. I know a pawnbroker who owes my Oma money. He'll talk — about the lumbago first, then everything else.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: And you found {echo} today. Keep it. Words are evidence too.

caseLine: The cradle has an author: O. Marsh, 1905. And the lining held a pawn ticket — Quayside, No. 77.

flavorChoice.dry: The harbor, then. Bring your lumbago sympathy.
flavorChoice.warm: The harbor, then. Buy the man some liniment on the way.
